name: Meetings & Pushback
lede: Say it without sounding rude. Learn the phrases for disagreeing, buying time, and moving a decision forward in a meeting where everyone is busy.
outcome: Say it without sounding rude. The words for disagreeing, buying time, and moving a decision forward.
outcomes: Disagree with an idea without making it personal — and keep the room on your side.
Buy time when you need to think, instead of filling the silence with “um”.
Move a stalled conversation toward a clear owner, decision, and next step.

aside.title: Built for the meeting you’re dreading.
aside.body: Every phrase is one you can say out loud without sounding stiff — or starting a fight.

words.definition: To use something you already have to get a better result.
words.example: We can leverage the data from last quarter.

words.definition: Disagreement or resistance to a plan or idea.
words.example: We got some pushback on the new timeline.

words.definition: To reach agreement on a plan, priority, or next step.
words.example: Let’s align on the scope before we start.

words.definition: To return to a topic later, usually after getting more information.
words.example: Let’s circle back on pricing after the client call.

words.definition: The time and energy someone has available for work.
words.example: I don’t have the bandwidth for a new project this month.

words.definition: Anyone affected by or interested in a project or decision.
words.example: We need sign-off from every stakeholder before the launch.

words.definition: A concrete result you promise to produce for a project.
words.example: The first deliverable is a one-page summary for the board.

words.definition: Agreement and support from the people who will be affected.
words.example: The plan works, but we still need buy-in from finance.

words.definition: The work included in a project, or the limits of what it covers.
words.example: That request is outside the scope of this sprint.

words.definition: The rhythm or frequency at which something happens.
words.example: Let’s agree on a weekly cadence for updates.

words.definition: The list of topics to discuss in a meeting.
words.example: Can you add that to the agenda for Thursday?

words.definition: The main point to remember from a meeting or talk.
words.example: My main takeaway is that we need more budget.

words.definition: To delay a topic until a later meeting.
words.example: Let’s park that idea until we have the numbers.

words.definition: To discuss something again later.
words.example: Let’s revisit the timeline next quarter.

words.definition: To point out a problem or risk so others notice it.
words.example: I want to flag a risk with the current plan.

words.definition: To bring a topic up for discussion.
words.example: I’d like to raise one concern about the deadline.

words.definition: A worry about something that might go wrong.
words.example: My main concern is the cost.

words.definition: A compromise where you accept one disadvantage to get an advantage.
words.example: The trade-off is speed versus quality.

words.definition: To disagree with or resist a plan.
words.example: Several people pushed back on the proposal.

words.definition: A warning or limit that you should know about.
words.example: There’s one caveat: the data is still incomplete.

words.definition: Something that two people or sides can agree on.
words.example: We found common ground on the launch date.

words.definition: An agreement where each side gives up a little.
words.example: We reached a compromise on the budget.

words.definition: A situation where no progress is possible because neither side will move.
words.example: The discussion ended in deadlock.

words.definition: To finish a meeting or discussion.
words.example: Let’s wrap up five minutes early.

words.definition: An action taken after a meeting to continue the work.
words.example: I’ll send a follow-up with the next steps.

words.definition: A specific task that someone agrees to do.
words.example: Let’s list the action items before we finish.

words.definition: The person responsible for a task or decision.
words.example: Every open question needs a clear owner.

words.definition: To include someone in a conversation or update.
words.example: Let’s loop in legal before we send this.

words.definition: To talk briefly to share updates.
words.example: Let’s touch base on Friday about progress.

words.definition: To wait before doing something.
words.example: Let’s hold off on hiring until Q2.

words.definition: To suggest an idea to see how people react.
words.example: I’ll float the idea in Monday’s meeting.

words.definition: A time when a meeting must end.
words.example: I have a hard stop at 3:15.
